claims.statement: Poland introduced virtual prosumer settlement in 2025 within one distribution operator and is extending it nationwide without the same-DSO restriction from 20 October 2026.

Property groups, municipalities, and renewable developers currently pay legal, metering, allocation, and settlement labor to coordinate generation and consumption points; actual project spend is unknown.
The likely payer is a property owner, cooperative, municipality, or developer seeking portfolio energy savings, but procurement authority and budget location are unverified.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Property asset manager, housing cooperative board, municipality, or renewable developer
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Energy sellers and developers can bundle settlement; independent scenario comparison, participant allocation, and audit trails provide resistance
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed project contracts with property groups or municipalities
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Renewable installers, property managers, energy advisers, and municipal procurement

fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Feasibility study prepaid; implementation milestones; recurring settlement fee
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 40-65% after legal, metering, and energy-market specialists
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Energy-law advice, metering integration, procurement, insurance, and data protection
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Feasibility and coordination fee plus recurring percentage or per-meter charge
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Specialist studies, meter data, settlement operations, and partner commissions

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Energy retailers, ESCOs, and developers offer turnkey virtual-prosumer coordination
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Current professional and staff time spent designing eligible structures, coordinating participants, obtaining data, and reconciling multi-point energy allocations
commercial_mechanics.payer: Property portfolio, housing cooperative, municipality, or renewable developer
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Nationwide eligibility, planned off-site PV project, or poor economics at a constrained onsite location
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Monthly settlement and annual participant or allocation review

contrary_evidence: Nationwide operation begins only on 20 October 2026, so transaction evidence is immature.
Energy-law and metering complexity may favor large incumbents.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed long-term coordination and data-rights contract among asset owner, participants, seller, and metering counterparties; unsigned
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Sell a one-off feasibility model without coordinating settlement or controlling project data
critical_control_point.current_owner: Asset owners, energy sellers, DSOs, and participants control the required assets, contracts, and meter data
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed project contracts with property groups or municipalities
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Family renewable-sector familiarity may support introductions under an explicit agreement, but no project, customer, or meter-data right is currently held
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business only after a multi-party mandate; counterparties retain legal and physical control
critical_control_point.subject: Multi-party virtual-prosumer coordination mandate

economics.acquisition_route: Sell five portfolio feasibility studies, identify one economically viable same-DSO or post-October project, then negotiate paid coordination
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: coordinating 100 projects averaging 100,000 PLN annual gross revenue yields 10m PLN revenue; at 15% owner earnings and recurring contract value, 5m PLN founder net worth is plausible in 7-12 years. Project conversion and regulation are major unknowns.
economics.founder_time: 20-25 hours weekly for feasibility; full projects require hired project management and licensed advisers
economics.gross_margin_basis: Coordination fees less specialist, acquisition, settlement, and project-management costs
economics.payback: Assumption: 18-30 months due to long project sales and coordination cycles
economics.pricing: Assumption: 15,000-50,000 PLN feasibility, 50,000-200,000 PLN implementation, and recurring per-meter fee
economics.retention_or_repeat: Multi-year once an operating project is established

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Allocation models, project benchmarks, and multi-party implementation playbooks
fingerprint.customer: Polish property portfolios and municipalities seeking off-site renewable allocation
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Asset owner pays professional coordination and ongoing settlement costs
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Virtual prosumer rules expand beyond a single DSO area

founder_fit: Energy analytics and family-sector context are relevant.
Feasibility studies can start part-time before heavier execution.
The model has larger contracts but also greater coordination intensity than preferred.
risks: The model is regulation- and counterparty-dependent.
Municipal and property sales cycles are long.
Multi-party coordination may conflict with the founder's social-energy preference.

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: multi party virtual prosumer project coordination
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: project level allocation and settlement mandate
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: nationwide virtual prosumer implementation and metering rules

thesis: Nationwide virtual-prosumer settlement creates a new coordination market for portfolios that cannot match renewable generation and consumption onsite.
title: Virtual Prosumer Project Coordinator
uncertainties: Feasible project savings and conversion rates are unknown.
Whether counterparties will grant a durable mandate is unknown.
